To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effective boundary conditions of the ground with the array of resonant plates/beams are of the Robin's (dynamic) type, and that these conditions are frequency dependent.
the presence of the slender bodies perturbs the propagation of elastic wave in the ground, which can be described by a frequency-dependent Robin's condition.
the effective model of the ground with an array of plates/beam can be obtained using asymptotic homogenization techniques.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the propagation of elastic wave in a semi-infinite ground supporting a dense array or plates/beams, which can be applied to the study of the propagation of elastic surface waves in the ground with a dense array of buried pipes.
the study of the propagation of waves on a semi-infinite homogeneous elastic medium, which is covered by an array of slender plates or beams.
the development of an effective model for the propagation of elastic surface waves in a substrate supporting an array of slender bodies (e.g., plates or beams) with flexural resonant frequencies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effective model provides a very good approximation of the full problem for the displacement fields and of the reflection coefficients, even in the case of high frequencies and high density of the plates, and for any incident angle.

the effective model provides accurate results at low and intermediate frequencies and that the effective boundary condition is able to reproduce the main features of the reflection coefficients at high frequency.
the proposed model is valid and reliable for the description of elastic waves propagating at oblique incidence in a substrate supporting an array of plates/beam with flexural resonant modes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the effective model is valid for a large class of incident waves (not limited to a plane wave) and that it can be used for any number of plates or beams, provided that the flexural resonances of the individual structures are not close to each other.
we have derived an effective model for the interaction of elastic waves propagating on a semi-infinite ground supporting a dense array plates/beams with low-frequency flexural resonance.
the effective model can be used to predict the reflection and transmission coefficients at low frequencies with the same accuracy as the direct numerical simulations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effective model is accurate for the reflection coefficients at all angles of incidence and for all frequency ranges of the incident wave.
the effect of an infinite number of plates/beams can be described in terms of the elastic ground alone.

the presence of a dense array of resonant plates/beams is equivalent to the presence of effective boundary conditions of the same type as the ones that would have resulted from the presence of a single resonant plate/beams, with an effective stiffness and an effective mass density that are both proportional to the number of resonant plates.
